title_en: The Limb of the Lustful Man
translit:
|| Ath Shri Kamika Ang ||20||

Parnarisun pritdi | jab tab hoy vinash ||
Ant vichhoho Jivana | hoy jagatman has ||1||
Gher narisun rusno | parnarisun prit ||
Ape samjego Jivana | jab andho athdego bhit ||2||
Nari sathe nehdo | kare so bado gamar ||
Lalopato kare Jivana | pan ant uthave kal ||3||
Nari sathe nehdo | te nar yahan na avsho ||
Apo raheshe tahan | abhadchhet na lavsho ||4||
Parnarisun pritdi | jaiso aganko nir ||
Gharki nari Jivana | shital gher gambhir ||5||
Jarakh lautani Jivana | par triyasu prit ||
Gadho na jane bapdo | jo chandan ladyo pith ||6||
Kukar chate had jyun | bhare larsu pet ||
Aiso jano Jivana | par triyasun het ||7||
Kami kapat taje Jivana | to pame Harika dham ||
Ape ap vagoiyun | pan saryo na eko kam ||8||
Kami narkun Jivana | Hari kabahun na deve thav ||
Bhitar rachi pachi kamini | baher dekhave bhav ||9||
Nari neh ja dakhavi | piyako chit hari ley ||
Bhav jalman bore Jivana | ta par paththar dey ||10||
Jab tuhi dahudash gai | rahu sant samagam sar ||
Sadguru sabde Jivana | utariye pele par ||11||

|| Iti Shri Kamika Ang sampurna ||20||
translation:
Here begins the Limb of the Lustful Man, 20.

1. Love for another man's wife brings ruin sooner or later; in the end comes separation, O Jivana, and one is made a laughing-stock in the world.

2. Sulking with the wife at home and loving another man's wife - he will understand it himself, O Jivana, when the blind man walks into the wall.

3. He who makes love with another's woman is a great fool; he fawns and flatters, O Jivana, but in the end death carries him off.

4. The man who has love-dealings with another's woman - let him not come here; let him keep his own self over there and not bring his defilement in.

5. Love for another man's wife is like water turned to fire; one's own wife at home, O Jivana, is cool and deep and steady.

6. Love for another's woman, O Jivana, is a hyena's wallowing; the poor donkey never knows that it is sandalwood loaded on its back.

7. As a dog gnaws a dry bone and fills its belly on its own drool - know such to be, O Jivana, affection for another's wife.

8. If the lustful man gives up his deceit, O Jivana, he attains Hari's abode; by his own doing he has disgraced himself, and not one purpose of his has been fulfilled.

9. To the lustful man, O Jivana, Hari never grants a place; inwardly he is steeped and soaked in the woman, while outwardly he displays devotion.

10. The woman only makes a show of love and steals away her lover's mind; she sinks him in the ocean of worldly existence, O Jivana, and lays a stone on top of him.

11. When the cry of "Thou, only Thou" has gone out in all ten directions, abide in the essence, the company of the saints; by the Satguru's shabd (word), O Jivana, one crosses to the farther shore.

|| Here ends the Limb of the Lustful Man, 20. ||
